title: Exact associated-sheaf chains transported to the projective line
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with its total-degree grading, $P=\operatorname{Proj}S$ [def-nagata-affine-proj], and $C:P\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ a chart-compatible isomorphism [def-sc-p1-proj-chart-isomorphism], with $\mathbf P^1_k$ as in [def-sc-p1-standard]. Let $M,A_0,A_1,A_2$ be integer-graded $S$-modules (internal direct-sum gradings, with $S_nM_j\subseteq M_{n+j}$ and likewise for each $A_i$). Suppose the degree-preserving maps give an exact sequence $0\to A_2\xrightarrow{f_2} A_1\xrightarrow{f_1} A_0\xrightarrow{f_0}M\to0$. Let $F$ be an associated sheaf of $M$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], specified by injective additive chart maps onto the degree-zero fractions on each positive homogeneous standard open, compatible with the degree-zero ring action and the localization restriction formula. Then there are associated sheaves $E_i$ of $A_i$, with these same three chart properties, and maps $g_2:(C^{-1})^*E_2\to(C^{-1})^*E_1$, $g_1:(C^{-1})^*E_1\to(C^{-1})^*E_0$, $g_0:(C^{-1})^*E_0\to(C^{-1})^*F$ on $\mathbf P^1_k$, with $g_2$ monic, $g_0$ epic and the chain exact at both middle terms. No freeness, finite-generation or coherence assumption is made.

source.place: Lemma 27.8.4, Tag 01M7, final paragraph; blueprint lem-sc-p1-graded-resolution, sheafification clause

proof.text: Decompose preimages into homogeneous components. Because the maps preserve degree and the gradings are internal, their images and kernels are graded. Put $K=\operatorname{range}(f_1)$. The supplied injectivity, range/kernel identities and surjectivity give $0\to A_2\to A_1\to K\to0$ and $0\to K\to A_0\to M\to0$. This is the image/kernel decomposition of the given chain, not a syzygy-existence assertion.
Construct the associated sheaves of the three A_i and K, retaining their injective chart maps onto degree-zero fractions and scalar/restriction formulas. The given F is used for M.

Induce the degree-preserving maps by the fraction formula. Apply exact associated sheafification to both short sequences, then splice through the sheaf of K. Functoriality identifies the middle map with the composite, giving monic and epic endpoints and exactness at both middle sheaves.

The pullback functors for C and its inverse are inverse equivalences: compose pullbackComp with pullbackCongr of the two scheme inverse identities, then pullbackId. An equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels, thus exact chains and monic/epic endpoints. Apply inverse pullback to the chain just constructed.
